A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSPCD research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original evaluations on eight real-world networks, including clustering scores, runtimes and parameter-sensitivity results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix G retain the real-world evaluations and add original synthetic-data recovery, imbalance-robustness and runtime-scaling results.

M1.justification: The regularized objective, Frank-Wolfe/local-search procedure and cached matrix updates in Algorithms 1–3 are retained. The new LSNaive and LSImproved runtime comparisons evaluate implementations already described in v1 Section 3.4.

E1.justification: V2 retains all eight real-world networks, including WoW-EP8 in the appendix, and adds synthetic networks with planted communities and neutral nodes. These introduce ground-truth recovery scenarios with controlled noise and balanced or imbalanced community sizes, absent from v1.

E2.justification: V2 adds the directly relevant balance-aware neural comparator N2PC, evaluated for k=2 on synthetic and real-world networks, including five gamma settings in the real-world comparisons. V1 only cited its underlying work. The existing SCG, KOCG, BNC and SPONGE comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: V2 replaces BAL and BA-polarity table metrics with the entropy-based imbalance factor, using xi=3, and introduces F1 recovery evaluation. New protocols vary synthetic noise, cluster-size ratios, graph size and cluster count, and sweep N2PC's gamma. The existing real-world ten-value beta selection procedure is retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds recovery analyses under noise and increasing ground-truth cluster imbalance, plus runtime comparisons isolating the benefits of the three existing implementations (Figures 1–3; Appendices G.4–G.5). The earlier alpha/beta sensitivity analyses remain, with revised balance reporting.

E5.justification: V2 specifies ten repetitions for the synthetic noise experiment and displays error bars in Figures 1–2 without defining their statistic. The real-world five-seed means and LSPCD standard-deviation reporting are retained; no increase in those runs is stated.

E6.justification: V2 adds imbalance-factor values, N2PC results, synthetic recovery curves and implementation-scaling measurements, while removing BAL/BA-polarity table entries. Retained metrics for the original methods are unchanged: for example, Bitcoin k=2 LSPCD polarity remains 29.022 in v1 Table 7 and v2 Table 5.

T1.justification: The formal balance criterion changes from a smallest/largest-cluster ratio and BA-polarity to normalized Renyi entropy in Section 4. The NP-hardness, equivalence, convergence and gradient proofs, beta-extreme proposition and polarity counterexample are retained after relocation.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly claims the first scalable local-search algorithm for PCD and adds ground-truth recovery to its stated empirical contributions. The central claims about balanced communities, efficient local search, its Frank-Wolfe connection and convergence rate remain.

C2.justification: New Appendices E–F substantially expand arguments about when balanced communities are useful and why additive regularization is preferable to gamma-polarity normalization. Section 4 explicitly discusses unavailable real-world ground truth and interprets synthetic robustness and N2PC's balance–polarity tradeoffs. The application examples are conceptual, not additional empirical studies.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses an Intel Core i9-10850k CPU and 64 GB RAM, documents synthetic edge-generation probabilities and cluster-size construction, and states that N2PC uses the authors' public implementation with default training parameters. Existing baseline implementation information is retained.

R1.justification: Gullo et al. (2024), already cited in v1, becomes a central comparison through explicit discussion of N2PC and gamma-polarity in the introduction and new Appendix F. V2 also adds He et al. (2022) and Pirizadeh et al. (2023), removes Chehreghani et al. (2012), and explicitly positions LSPCD as the first scalable local-search approach for PCD.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, problem motivation and conclusion are substantially rewritten. CC/PCD propositions and the alpha/beta discussion move into dedicated appendices, proofs are reordered, and the experimental supplement is reorganized into focused subsections. Citation style also changes from author–year to numbered references.

P2.justification: V2 adds three experimental figures and a dedicated N2PC comparison table, redesigns result tables around joint polarity/imbalance reporting, and relocates the earlier parameter plots as Figures 4–5, updating Figure 4's balance panel. The document template, author block, algorithm placement and table scaling also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V1 relied on real-world proxy scores and omitted an evaluated comparison with N2PC. V2 adds planted-ground-truth recovery under noise and imbalance, direct measurements of implementation speedups, and the relevant neural baseline (Figures 1–3 and Table 2). These substantially strengthen validation of the central quality and scalability claims despite unchanged original scores. Real-world ground truth remains unavailable, and the new error bars are insufficiently explained.
